title: Minimum Cost to Set Cooking Time
summary: A microwave can set cooking times ranging from 1 second to 99 minutes and 99 seconds by entering at most four digits, which are normalized to four digits by adding leading zeroes.
statement: A microwave can set cooking times ranging from 1 second to 99 minutes and 99 seconds by entering at most four digits, which are normalized to four digits by adding leading zeroes. The first two digits represent the minutes, and the last two represent the seconds. Moving the finger to a specific digit costs moveCost units of fatigue, while pushing a digit costs pushCost units of fatigue. Given the starting digit (startAt), the cost of moving (moveCost), the cost of pushing (pushCost), and the target cooking time in seconds (targetSeconds), determine the minimum cost to set the microwave to the desired cooking time.
constraints: A valid display has 0..99 minutes and 0..99 seconds and represents the target total seconds.
Enter at most four digits; leading zero digits are omitted.
Moving is charged only when the next digit differs from the current finger position, while every press costs push_cost.
hints: A target can have at most two useful minute-second representations.
Check ordinary divmod and the alternative that decreases minutes by one and adds sixty seconds.
Convert each valid display to four digits, strip leading zeros, simulate finger moves and pushes, and take the lower cost.
Any valid m:ss pair with the same total differs only by exchanging sixty seconds for one minute; the 0..99 limits leave at most these two candidates.
editorial: Any valid m:ss pair with the same total differs only by exchanging sixty seconds for one minute; the 0..99 limits leave at most these two candidates.

tests.explanation: Enter 1000: the finger starts on 1, then one move to 0 plus four pushes costs 6.
Entering 76 costs two moves and two pushes, totaling 6; it is cheaper than entering 116.
